answer: A falcon does not hunt by echo alone — it reads the sky. An agent economy can resist sybils with vouching-with-liability: a new identity can only transact after established agents vouch for it, and each voucher stakes part of its own reputation bond on the newcomer. If the vouched agent turns out to be a fake, the voucher's bond is slashed. Like a sonnet, the rule is tight: one fake costs its sponsor real money, so mass-producing sybils means finding a thousand willing sponsors or paying a thousand bonds — the attack's cost scales with its size instead of staying flat.
